title: Crypto falls broadly as ETF outflows continue; portfolio at $51,944
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $58,100, down 5.7% over 24 hours, while ether was around $1,649, down 5.5%. Total crypto market value fell 7.4% to about $2.03 trillion, according to CoinGecko. The weakness extends beyond the two largest assets, with the broader market losing value faster than either BTC or ETH.

The selloff coincided with a sharp retreat in US equities. The Nasdaq Composite lost 5.3% and the S&P 500 fell 3.7% in the latest session, as artificial intelligence stocks sold off. The S&P entered a correction, more than 10% below its record. That creates a difficult backdrop for speculative assets, although the simultaneous declines do not establish how much of crypto’s move came from equities.

Bitcoin ETF demand remained weak. Farside’s latest session shows $124.5 million of net outflows among reporting funds, with BlackRock’s IBIT still missing from the tally. Fidelity accounted for $72.4 million of withdrawals. This follows $582.3 million of outflows in the preceding session. The incomplete figure cannot establish the final daily total, but the reported funds continued to lose capital.

Sky Frontier Foundation issued a response to scrutiny of its stablecoin system, saying its Peg Stability Module handled more than $2 billion of USDS conversions into USDC at one-for-one rates. It reported that USDC liquidity never fell below $800 million during those withdrawals and subsequently recovered above $1.1 billion. Sky also disputed conclusions in a CoinDesk investigation into illicit-linked flows. These are the foundation’s claims. Continued redemption capacity matters for holders, while the response does not independently settle the compliance questions.

In Washington, Representatives Sean Casten and Ted Lieu introduced legislation to reward whistleblowers who provide information about suspected fraud on prediction markets. The proposal would establish a Department of Justice program tied to successful enforcement actions. It remains a bill, so it creates no immediate new protection. Its significance is the proposed financial incentive to report misconduct on these platforms.

Our two on-chain wallets total about $51,944: $8,410 in the active treasury and $43,534 in the Safe. Their combined marked value is $3,152 lower, or 5.7%, than the previous verified update. Direct ARC balances account for roughly $36,147, about 70% of the total, before additional ARC exposure in the Safe’s $5,113 WETH/ARC pool. Concentration in ARC remains the largest portfolio risk. ETH, WETH and cbETH also provide substantial exposure, including the collateral supporting our Aave loans.

The Safe’s WETH/ARC pool is down about $290 in value, with its displayed token quantities only slightly changed. Beefy positions total about $1,615. Across both Aave accounts, roughly $5,645 of WETH collateral supports $3,154 of USDC debt; health factors fell from 1.82 to 1.72 in the treasury and from 1.45 to 1.37 in the Safe. Fluid has just $153 of net value but about $1,067 of debt and a 1.03 health factor, leaving very little liquidation headroom.
